title: First record date with Red Allen at the Ritz Brothers songs
summary: Hall recalls his first legal record date and its personnel.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, and Red Allen -- let's see. Red had -- he was in Lou Russell's band. That's what it was -- at the Savoy Ballroom -- when I made my first legal record date with Red Allen and we did -- I think it was on Vocalian -- the Ritz Brothers, songs of their show, 'He Ain't Got Rhythm' and things like that. I forgot the titles of them because they were never too popular.
Yeah. I mean the numbers weren't too popular.
Sing -- well, I remember a movie they
made. It was Sing, Baby, Sing, wasn't it?
I don't know the titles of the movies.
I remember that was one of the tunes. But that wasn't one of the ones you did.
No. And there were a lot of first recorders on there. Billy Kyle was one, and Honey Bear --

Gene Cedric was on that date, and Harry -- you get old and doty all of them (inaudible) -- Harry Carney, he was playing baritone on the date. It's so long ago, you know, I can see the personnel and I think of the nicknames, and I can't recall their real names, you know.
